title: Traffic-shape generators + cache warmup phase + baseline artifact packaging
author: Rina Kobayashi
body:
Summary: This PR adds first-class traffic-shape generators (prompt length distributions + concurrency ramps), introduces an explicit cache warmup phase to standardize warm/cold runs, and adds baseline artifact packaging so a given run can be rehydrated and rerun later with identical inputs. This is a prerequisite for locking the Q1 2026 baseline suite (ENG-4822) and versioning artifacts (ENG-4823).

Motivation / context: As we started validating repeatability across regions/hardware, we kept seeing subtle drift caused by (a) ad-hoc generation of prompt lengths and concurrency patterns inside individual workloads and (b) inconsistent cache state between runs. This PR centralizes those knobs into generators with explicit seed handling and a consistent warmup strategy, and produces a portable artifact bundle for each run.

What’s included (high level): 1) Prompt length distribution generators: - new schema section: traffic_shape.prompt_tokens and traffic_shape.output_tokens - supported distributions: fixed, uniform, discrete_weighted, lognormal, bimodal_lognormal - supports min/max clamps + integer rounding to match tokenizer behavior - deterministic sampling: seed + stream_id derived per request (stable across concurrency changes) 2) Concurrency ramps: - new schema section: traffic_shape.concurrency - supported ramps: constant, step, linear, staircase, poisson_bursts - ramp is expressed in terms of target inflight requests; runner uses a token-bucket + per-request admission loop to approximate the target while respecting backpressure 3) Cache warmup phase: - optional phases[] per workload: warmup + measure (+ optional cooldown) - warmup controls: duration_s OR requests, cache_mode: cold|warm_prefix|warm_kv (runtime-dependent) - warm_prefix mode uses a prompt prefix reuse mechanism (configurable prefix_pool) to drive realistic prefix/KV cache hits without storing customer prompts - measurement phase can assert a minimum cache_hit_rate window when warm modes are used (for CI sanity checks) 4) Baseline artifact packaging: - runner now writes a "run bundle" alongside results.json: run_bundle.tgz containing: workload YAML/JSON (resolved), prompt set (if synthetic), seeds, generator params, runner version, git SHA (if available), and environment capture stub (driver/CUDA placeholders filled by infra runner) - adds a stable bundle_id = sha256(resolved_workload + seeds + generator params + runner version) - adds CLI: benchmark-lab pack --input results_dir --output bundle.tgz and benchmark-lab replay --bundle bundle.tgz (reconstructs resolved workload + seeds)

CLI examples: - Generate a representative long-context streaming shape with a ramp and warmup: benchmark-lab run --workload workloads/q1_2026/streaming_long_context.yaml --set traffic_shape.prompt_tokens=bimodal_lognormal --set traffic_shape.concurrency=staircase --set phases[0].type=warmup --set phases[0].cache_mode=warm_prefix --seed 1337 - Pack artifacts: benchmark-lab pack --input out/run_2026-01-31T0212Z --output out/run_2026-01-31T0212Z/run_bundle.tgz - Replay: benchmark-lab replay --bundle out/run_2026-01-31T0212Z/run_bundle.tgz --runner-args "--region us-east-1 --hardware h100"

Not included / follow-ups: - No production telemetry integration here; this is workload definition + runner behavior only. - Hardware normalization (pinning driver/CUDA + instance fingerprinting) will be handled in the multi-region runner PR (ENG-4825). - Additional traffic shapes (mixed tenants, mixed models per run) will come via workload composition, not in this PR.

Implementation notes: - Determinism: sampling uses a splitmix64 RNG (pure Python implementation) with explicit seed per request_id; request_id is derived from (trial_id, phase_id, logical_request_idx) so varying target concurrency does not reshuffle lengths. - Output schema: results.json now includes traffic_shape_resolved (serialized) and phases_summary for traceability. - Cardinality control: concurrency generator emits only summarized counters; per-request per-tick series are not exported (see review notes).

Files / areas changed: - src/traffic_shape/generators.py: prompt/output token distribution implementations - src/traffic_shape/concurrency.py: inflight target generator + admission controller - src/workload/schema.py: schema extensions: traffic_shape.*, phases[] - src/runner/phases.py: warmup/measure/cooldown orchestration - src/artifacts/packaging.py: run_bundle.tgz creation + replay loader - workloads/examples/*: new example workloads demonstrating distributions/ramps/warmup - tests/test_traffic_shape_generators.py: deterministic sampling + distribution sanity checks - tests/test_packaging_roundtrip.py: bundle_id stability + replay equivalence

Commits (squash summary): - Add prompt/output token distribution generators and seed plumbing - Add concurrency ramp generators and inflight admission controller - Add workload phases (warmup/measure/cooldown) with cache warmup options - Add run bundle packaging + replay command - Add tests + example workloads + docs

Review conversation (highlights): - Claire Dubois: "Can we ensure the bimodal distribution doesn’t accidentally overrepresent ultra-long prompts due to clamp/rounding?" Author: Adjusted clamp semantics to apply pre-rounding and added a histogram-based test to assert tail bounds. - Sana Farid: "We need determinism under different concurrency schedules; otherwise variance work will be noisy." Author: Changed request_id derivation to exclude wall-clock scheduling and added test that identical seeds produce identical sampled lengths when ramp type changes. - Thomas Baird: "Please avoid exporting per-tick concurrency series into results.json; it’ll explode metrics/cardinality downstream." Author: Removed per-tick series from default output; kept an optional --debug-trace flag that writes a local CSV only. - Marcus Reed: "Bundle should include the fully resolved workload, not the human-authored one, so we can reproduce overrides." Author: Packaging now always writes resolved_workload.json with all defaults and --set overrides applied.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for generators and replay - [x] Example workloads added - [x] Backwards compatibility: existing workloads without traffic_shape/phases continue to run (defaults to single measure phase, fixed token lengths) - [x] Docs: README section "Traffic shapes" + "Run bundles" - [x] Linked to ENG-4822/4823/4826

CI: - benchmark-lab / unit-tests: pass - benchmark-lab / lint: pass - benchmark-lab / typecheck: pass - benchmark-lab / integration-smoke (workload run + pack + replay): pass

Release notes: Adds traffic-shape generators, warmup phases, and run bundle packaging/replay to support Q1 2026 performance baseline reproducibility.
